title: query_dataset ObjectQL face: push the top-N order-and-cut to the database (SQL-first) instead of fetching every group
body:
repo:objectstack#5 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CbUb7TcZK1XUAddUmQ

Filing gate: split from #35204 by seat 5 (route ruling on #35204; dev report 6997512051 option C). ⛔ Not a claim.

## What

On the ObjectQL face (date buckets, `$field` filters, external objects, drivers without raw SQL) `query_dataset` fetches every group and cuts top-N in memory (`strategies/objectql-strategy.ts:815` `orderAndWindow` → `applyWindow(applyOrdering(...))`). `totalGroups` is already exact there (whole-grid length, `dataset-group-count.ts:107`), so correctness holds; the gap is AGENTS.md Prime Directive 5 (SQL-first) on compiling drivers: a large grouping is read whole to return N rows.

The engine already has the order-and-cut (`packages/objectql/src/aggregate-order-cut.ts`, `AGGREGATE_ORDER_CUT`, zero callers), but the face cannot reach it: its read seam `ctx.executeAggregate` carries no read option, and the engine refuses (400) rather than declines where it cannot serve the cut.

## Routes (from the #35204 dev report, costs are estimates)

- A: objectql gains an opt-in `declined` outcome (nothing read) like the relation group join; service-analytics adds an order-cut read seam and the strategy sends `orderBy` + `limit = offset + limit`. Two packages, ~300–450 lines.
- B: consumer only, catching the engine's pre-read 400 and falling back. One package, ~250–350 lines; discriminates refusals by error fields.

## Needs a maintainer decision before build

A and B both change which rows a text-ordered top-N returns on compiling drivers (database collation and NULL placement instead of `applyOrdering`). That is visible behaviour. The seat brings route and ordering to the maintainer with an analysis before dispatch.

## Done when

On a compiling driver the face reads only the cut rows from the database, `totalGroups` stays exact, the ordering rule the maintainer picks is pinned, and an engine that cannot serve the cut falls back without a refusal reaching the user.
